gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the longest one-piece print-in-place fidget each bed can hold. The A1 mini's 180 mm bed has a 254.6 mm diagonal, so a 200 mm articulated dragon fits only if it is laid diagonally and is no wider than 54.6 mm. The A1's 256 mm bed holds it straight and has a 362.0 mm diagonal.
standout_why: Compared against four pages. 3dprintgearlab (rank 1) gives bed area and cost per mm² for the A1 mini (32,400 mm²) and P1S (65,536 mm²) but not diagonals or any longest-part limit. extruly (cited) mentions '200 mm dragons' that take 4–5 h on an A1 mini, but never explains how a 200 mm part fits on a 180 mm bed; it states a 180 × 180 mm plate and no diagonal. aemind (cited) gives dragon print times (4 h 42 min on a P1S) and 'about a dollar' of filament per toy, but no model sizes or bed-fit limits. Tom's Hardware (cited) came back truncated twice, so I could not check it.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's A1 mini pick for typical fidgets: spinners, gear rings and 120 mm dragons fit straight on its 180 mm bed. It also sets a hard switch point. Any print-in-place piece longer than 180 mm has to go diagonally on the mini, and the length plus width must stay at or under 254.6 mm. A long snake or a wide-winged 200 mm dragon will not fit, so those buyers need the A1 (256 mm straight, 362 mm diagonal). The A1 also has 2.02× the bed area, roughly twice the fidgets per batch, which matters for selling.
candidates: Bambu Lab A1 mini Combo (AMS lite)
